title: Ukrainian drones set two Samara refineries ablaze hours after Putin vows 'inevitable' retaliation
dek: Putin told his energy commission that Kyiv was ignoring Donald Trump's request to stop hitting refineries. Ukraine's foreign minister told him to end the war instead.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Ukrainian drones set fire to two of Russia's large oil refineries in the Samara region overnight into Wednesday, hours after President Vladimir Putin told his country's top energy executives that Russian "retaliatory measures" against Kyiv were "inevitable". Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, replied that Mr Putin could stop the strikes by ending the war.

The attacks, about 800 km from the front line, hit the Syzran and Kuibyshev refineries, both owned by the state-controlled Rosneft, according to footage analysed by an independent Russian media outlet and cited in reports. The Samara governor, Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said air defences and mobile fire groups had destroyed more than 145 drones over the region and that one person had been killed, with power cut in some areas. He did not name the plants. Russia's defence ministry said it shot down 305 Ukrainian drones over 14 regions overnight. None of these figures can be independently verified.

## What happened

Mr Putin spoke on Tuesday at a meeting of the presidential Commission for Strategic Development of the Fuel and Energy Sector, whose executive secretary is Rosneft's chief executive, Igor Sechin. According to the Kremlin's transcript, he said that "the Kiev regime has not stopped its attacks on our oil refining infrastructure – and this is despite the call and direct request from the President of the United States to refrain from such attacks."

"Let me be clear on this: retaliatory measures on our part are inevitable, and everyone should be aware of that," he said. He added that the Ukrainian escalation that began in early June "cannot inflict critical damage on us", but asked the commission to discuss "what further steps are needed to strengthen the security of our oil refineries and to protect the people who work there".

He also told the meeting that Russia had restricted exports of petrol and jet fuel, and of diesel "with the exception of partial supplies to global markets, as agreed with the President of the United States", and that petrol prices had "mostly stabilised" after peaking in early October. "The current situation in the petroleum products market remains difficult," he said.

Within hours, the Samara refineries were burning. Ukrainian monitoring channels also reported explosions near the Novokuibyshevsk refinery and a pumping station run by the pipeline company Transneft in the same region, but there was no visual confirmation of damage there, reports said. Ukraine's General Staff had not commented on the Samara strikes by Wednesday afternoon.

Mr Sybiha responded on social media on Tuesday. "If Putin doesn't like Ukraine's strikes on his oil refineries, he can order an end to the war," he wrote, adding: "Stop complaining. End the war."

## The other side of the night

Russia kept up its own attacks on Ukraine. Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 112 drones overnight into Wednesday, 66 of them Shahed-type attack drones, and that 88 had been shot down or suppressed by 8 am local time (11.30 am IST), with hits recorded at 18 locations. No missiles were reported.

In Bila Tserkva, south of Kyiv, a 52-year-old man was killed and a shopping store and a parcel depot were hit, the Kyiv regional governor, Tymur Tkachenko, said, according to reports. In Kyiv, a drone struck the courtyard of a 16-storey residential block late on Tuesday, injuring two people, the State Emergency Service said. Across Ukraine, local authorities reported nine people killed and 77 injured in Russian attacks on Tuesday, according to a tally compiled from regional statements; Ukrainian and Russian figures for casualties and damage are not independently verified.

## Background

Ukraine has made Russia's oil refineries the main target of its long-range drone campaign this year. Ukraine has struck 16 Russian refineries since early November alone, according to reports, and one independent tracker counts strikes on 29 of Russia's 33 crude refineries since the campaign widened. Industry sources cited in reports said Russian refining volumes fell 45% in the first three weeks of November. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in mid-November that Ukraine's strikes had disabled more than 55% of Russia's refining capacity, a figure Moscow has not accepted.

Syzran, one of the two plants hit on Wednesday, has a capacity of about 8.9 million tonnes of crude a year and Kuibyshev about 7 million tonnes, reports said. Both were struck in September as well; Ukraine's General Staff said at the time that the Syzran strike had forced the plant to suspend operations.

In September, President Donald Trump asked Kyiv to stop hitting Russian refineries, saying the attacks were hurting the world as fuel disruptions from the Ukraine war and the conflict with Iran pushed US diesel prices to a record. Moscow welcomed the request. Kyiv argues the refineries fund Russia's war and that its strikes answer Russian attacks on Ukraine's power grid, which its allies fear will leave Ukrainians facing another winter of blackouts.

The night's exchanges come days after Ukrainian drones hit Russian vessels in the Gulf of Finland and off Libya, which Moscow condemned as a dangerous widening of the war.

## Why it matters for India

India is one of the largest buyers of Russian seaborne crude. Damage to Russia's refineries cuts the amount of crude Russia can process at home, which tends to leave more crude for export, while Russia's limits on fuel exports reduce the supply of diesel and petrol on world markets. Both feed into the prices Indian refiners pay and the margins they earn on fuel.

Mr Putin also pointed his industry east. "Given the current trajectory of our relations with Asia-Pacific nations and the growing demand from our Asian partners, we must expand transport infrastructure capacity across Siberia and the Far East," he said, calling for "particular attention" to oil refining and petrochemicals in eastern Russia, and for wider use of the Northern Sea Route. He repeated that efforts in Europe to restrict Russian energy imports would leave Europeans with "less of our oil and gas and more problems".

Global prices were easing on Wednesday: Brent crude was around $91 a barrel during Indian trading hours, reports said, which helped lift Indian shares.

## What happens next

Mr Putin did not say what form the retaliation would take. Ukraine's power grid and gas production sites have been the main targets of Russia's large strikes in recent weeks, and Ukrainian officials have warned of further mass attacks as temperatures fall. Rosneft has not said how long repairs at Syzran and Kuibyshev will take.

## Key numbers

- 145+: drones the Samara governor said were destroyed over his region overnight
- 305: Ukrainian drones Russia's defence ministry said it downed over 14 regions
- 112: Russian drones Ukraine's air force said were launched at Ukraine; 88 downed
- 45%: reported fall in Russian refining volumes in the first three weeks of November (industry sources)
- 16: Russian refineries reported hit by Ukraine since early November
